source.title: Étude in G♭ major, Op. 10 No. 5

humdrumCorrections.basis: Source token correction with print reference: 010-1b-Sm-005.krn line 91 (bar 4, under 8va) encodes the middle note of the last right-hand triplet as `24dad-`, which contains two pitch names and is not a valid **kern pitch; read as D-flat6 (`24ddd-`). Print, viewed 19 Oct 2026 in OCVE page images: the French first edition (10-1-Sm, M. Schlesinger, p. 20, bar 4, the first bar of the second system; https://chopinonline.ac.uk/ocve/browse/pageview/63226/) engraves this group under 8a as A-flat above the staff, D-flat on the fourth line, D-flat above the staff, i.e. sounding A-flat6, D-flat6, D-flat7. The encoding's parallel bar 12 has the same group as `24aaa-` / `24ddd-` / `24dddd-` (lines 223-226). The downloaded bytes are unchanged; the correction is applied in memory and retained in the check report.

Source token correction with print reference: 010-1b-Sm-005.krn line 788 (bar 47, under 8va) encodes the middle note of the last right-hand triplet as `24ede-` (two pitch names); read as E-flat6 (`24eee-`), between the D-flat6 notes of lines 787/789. Print, viewed 19 Oct 2026: French first edition (10-1-Sm, M. Schlesinger, p. 22, bar 47; https://chopinonline.ac.uk/ocve/browse/pageview/63228/) engraves every lower triplet of the bar under 8a as D-flat, E-flat, D-flat (one staff step up and back), the last one included. The bar's other three groups are encoded `24dddd-`/`24eeee-`/`24dddd-` and `24ddd-`/`24eee-`/`24ddd-` (lines 776-786). The downloaded bytes are unchanged; the correction is applied in memory and retained in the check report.

Source token correction with print reference: 010-1b-Sm-005.krn line 1357 (bar 83, first right-hand chord, last note under 8va) encodes the upper chord member as `24gbg-'` (two pitch names) beside `24bb-`; read as G-flat6 (`24ggg-'`). Print, viewed 19 Oct 2026: French first edition (10-1-Sm, M. Schlesinger, p. 24, bar 83; https://chopinonline.ac.uk/ocve/browse/pageview/63230/) engraves this staccato sixteenth chord at the end of the 8a line as G-flat in the space above the treble staff with B-flat on the middle line, i.e. sounding G-flat6/B-flat5, over the left hand's G-flat4. The downloaded bytes are unchanged; the correction is applied in memory and retained in the check report.

bars.description: Bars 1-85 once in written order. The source has no repeat signs; nothing is cut or repeated. Bar 85 holds the closing G-flat whole notes as printed (four quarters in a 2/4 bar), not clamped.

end.basis: MEAS: the display end of Op. 10 No. 5 on this two-étude side. After the final G-flat chord (92.67 s) its bands decay into the transfer's surface noise by 94.6 s (F-sharp4 -48 dB, F-sharp3 -52 dB; total -18.6 dB, the same as the noise-only gap 94.7-96.3 s). Op. 25 No. 9 begins at 96.4 s (its opening B-flat4 jumps -30 -> -10 dB at 96.4 s), and the rest of the side is not covered by this score. This is not a measured key release; the whole-file -45 dB RMS end lies after Op. 25 No. 9.

endpoints.basis: MEAS, cached pitch features (dB re the 95th-percentile total) and the fresh overlay work/chopin-etude-op10-5-cortot-0-11.7.png. First: the transfer is digitally quiet to 0.7 s; groove noise (MIDI 25-40 rumble and a flat -40 dB high band, total about -21 dB) starts at 0.8-0.9 s, but the first musical attack, the right hand's G-flat6 with the left-hand G-flat chord (q0), rises at 3.66-3.74 s (F-sharp4 -30 -> -11 dB, total -15 -> -6 dB, first large DLNCO peak), followed by B-flat6 3.76, D-flat6 3.88 and G-flat6 3.96 s. The broad 0-3 s first-pass window chose 2.86 s, inside the groove noise. Last: bar 85's G-flat1/G-flat2/G-flat3 whole notes (q168) rise at 92.6-92.7 s (F-sharp4 -32 -> -9 dB, F-sharp3 -44 -> -25 dB; primary onset 92.682 s), after the high G-flat chord of bar 84 (q167; A-sharp4/A-sharp5/F-sharp6 jump at 91.8-91.9 s) and the descending bar-83/84 octaves. The broad 85-96 s window chose 91.28 s, the bar-84 G-flat octave.

anchors.label: bar-64-chord
anchors.basis: MEAS, cached pitch features: bar 64 (q126), the lower staff's G-flat4/A-flat4/D-flat5 with the right hand's D-flat6, rises at 68.04-68.12 s (C-sharp5 band -17 -> -2 dB, F-sharp4 -29 -> -19 dB, total -11 -> -1 dB); detector edge 68.06 s, primary and adaptive onset 68.000 s. The round-4 map (68.07 s) was already right here. This constraint keeps it there: a dry run with only the q131-q138 constraints moved q126 to 69.49 s and opened a 1.1 s gap inside bar 63 (q125.333 67.75 s, q125.5 68.87 s).

anchors.label: bar-65-chord
anchors.basis: MEAS: the bar-65 chord D-flat3/A-flat3/D-flat4/G-flat4 with the right hand's E-flat7 (q128) rises at 69.48-69.60 s (F-sharp4 -50 -> -31 dB, C-sharp5 partial -35 -> -28 dB, C-sharp4 -48 -> -39 dB by 69.64 s); detector edge 69.48 s, adaptive onset 69.544 s. The round-4 map (69.547 s) was right; the dry run with only the q131-q138 constraints moved it to 70.547 s. The bar's descending sextuplets then sound from E-flat6 (q128.833) at 70.46 s to D-flat5 (q129.833, C-sharp5 -42 -> -21 dB) at 71.00 s.

anchors.label: bar-66-chord
anchors.basis: MEAS: the bar-66 Smorz. chord D-flat3/A-flat3/C-flat4/E-flat4/G-flat4 with the right hand's A-flat4 (q130) rises at 71.46-71.56 s (G-sharp4 -40 -> -25 dB, F-sharp4 -52 -> -28 dB); detector edge 71.48 s, adaptive onset 71.471 s, 0.86 s before the q131 B-flat4. Round-4 map 71.383 s; the dry run with only the q131-q138 constraints put it at 71.603 s.

anchors.label: bar-66-B-flat4
anchors.basis: MEAS, cached pitch features (dB re the 95th-percentile total): after the bar-66 Smorz. chord (q130, edge 71.48 s), the right hand's B-flat4 dotted eighth with the left hand's D-flat4/F4 (q131) rises at 72.30-72.36 s (A-sharp4 band -41 -> -15 dB; F4 -52 -> -33 dB at 72.40-72.48 s); detector edge 72.34 s, adaptive onset 72.307 s. The B-flat4 is held, decaying to about -33 dB, past the A-flat4 sixteenth (q131.75; G-sharp4 -48 -> -28 dB at 73.08-73.16 s, edge 73.10 s) until the bar-67 G-flat4. The round-4 map put q131 at 71.936 s and q131.75 at 72.348 s, leaving no room for this hold (RevScoresChopin review, defect BARS_67_69_LIT_ABOUT_1S_EARLY).

anchors.label: bar-66-A-flat4
anchors.basis: MEAS: the bar-66 A-flat4 sixteenth (q131.75) rises at 73.08-73.16 s under the sustained B-flat4 (G-sharp4 band -48 -> -28 dB, G-sharp5 partial -46 -> -35 dB; A-sharp4 still -28 to -33 dB until 73.44 s); detector edge 73.10 s, adaptive onset 73.073 s. No other score note has A-flat4 between q131 and bar 67's q133 (C-flat4/A-flat4 at 74.06 s). With the other constraints but not this one, the map put q131.75 at 73.348 s, 0.25 s late; the round-4 map had 72.348 s.

anchors.label: bar-67-G-flat4
anchors.basis: MEAS: the a-tempo bar-67 downbeat, right-hand G-flat4 with the left hand's G-flat3/B-flat3/G-flat4 (q132), rises at 73.44-73.52 s (F-sharp4 band -45 -> -30 dB, F-sharp5 partial -42 -> -35 dB) as the B-flat4 hold falls from -33 to -43 dB; detector edge 73.48 s, adaptive onset 73.538 s. The rest of the bar follows: C-flat4/A-flat4 with A-flat6 (q133; G-sharp4 -41 -> -26 dB) at 74.06 s, B-flat6 at 74.12-74.16 s, then A-flat3/F4 with D-flat6 (q133.5; C-sharp6 -40 -> -23 dB, F4 -45 -> -28 dB) at 74.30 s and D-flat7 at 74.36 s. Published 72.48 s.

anchors.label: bar-68-D-flat6
anchors.basis: MEAS: bar 68 (q134), the right hand's D-flat6 with G-flat3/B-flat3/G-flat4, rises at 74.52-74.58 s (F-sharp4 -44 -> -25 dB, C-sharp6 -32 -> -21 dB, F-sharp3 -53 -> -42 dB by 74.66 s); detector edge 74.54 s, adaptive onset 74.501 s. The next sextuplet note E-flat6 (q134.167) rises -40 -> -21 dB at 74.60-74.66 s, then G-flat5 with D-flat4 (q134.5) at 74.78 s, A-flat5 with C-flat4/A-flat4 (q135) at 75.04 s and B-flat5 at 75.10 s. The earlier D-flat6 rise at 74.30 s is bar 67's q133.5 (with F4 and the D-flat7 of q133.667): E-flat6 stays at -40 to -42 dB until 74.60 s, so bar 68 does not start at 74.3 s. Published 73.537 s.

anchors.label: bar-68-D-flat5
anchors.basis: MEAS: the bar-68 D-flat5 quarter with A-flat3/F4 (q135.5) is the loudest attack in 70.8-77.6 s: C-sharp5 band -24 -> -5 dB at 75.22-75.30 s (total -14 -> -4 dB); detector edge 75.26 s, primary and adaptive onset 75.244 s. It follows the A-flat5/B-flat5/A-flat5 sextuplets at 75.04/75.10/75.20 s. Published 74.33 s.

anchors.label: bar-69-left-hand
anchors.basis: MEAS: bar 69 opens with the left hand alone (q136, G-flat3/B-flat3/G-flat4) under the held D-flat5; F-sharp4 band -47 -> -33 dB at 75.50-75.62 s, detector edge 75.54 s, adaptive onset 75.569 s. The right-hand figure follows: G-flat5 (q136.167) at 75.62-75.70 s, A-flat5 75.74-75.78, B-flat5 75.82-75.86, A-flat5 75.94 and G-flat5 75.98 s, then D-flat5 with F3/C-flat4/E-flat4 (q137) at 76.04 s, A-flat5 76.18 s, D-flat6 76.26 s and E-flat6 with D-flat3/D-flat4 (q137.5) at 76.28 s. Published 74.71 s, which left this complete second run without a score position.

anchors.label: bar-70-G-flat5
anchors.basis: MEAS: the bar-70 downbeat G-flat5 with G-flat3/B-flat3/E-flat4 (q138) rises at 76.50-76.58 s (F-sharp5 -43 -> -18 dB, D-sharp4 -41 -> -24 dB, F-sharp3 -56 -> -41 dB by 76.62 s); detector edge 76.52 s, adaptive onset 76.579 s. Bar 71 (q140, G-flat3/B-flat3/G-flat4 with G-flat6) follows at 77.52 s (edge), where the round-4 map (77.508 s) already lies; it is not constrained. Published 76.311 s.

Edition: the Paris first edition of Études Op. 10 (M. Schlesinger), catalogued by NIFC Chopin First Editions Online as 010-1b-Sm-005 (RISM 300605128, PL-Wbfc 1628/n); encoding Tomasz Sierawski, editing Jędrzej Mróz and Emilia Ziętek. The performer's edition is not established; first-edition readings can differ from later editions.

Conversion: tools/align/humdrum_convert.py reads the unchanged **kern tokens (Humdrum line timing, spine splits/merges, explicit sounding pitches, ties, graces, tuplets) and writes plain MusicXML for the pinned LilyPond 2.24.4 converter. Dynamics, hairpins, pedalling, fingering, stems, layout comments, *rscale display scaling, cue size and editorial text are not converted; slurs are kept only when both ends lie in one encoded voice. Voices are the encoded Humdrum sub-spines on each staff (MusicXML voices 1-4 upper, 5-8 lower), labelled here only as upper/lower staff.

Recording: Alfred Cortot, Victor 64989 (matrix B-23953, take 2), Camden, 22 April 1920; acoustic. The disc side continues with Op. 25 No. 9 (from about 96.5 s), which this Op. 10 No. 5 score does not cover (content/listen module).
